reports.title: B2Gold Reports Q3 2026 Results - Lowers Annual All-In Sustaining Cost Guidance and Remains On-Track to Achieve Production Guidance

guidance.heading: Outlook
section: Consolidated gold production was 634,732 ounces in the first nine months of 2026. Strong year-to-date production from Masbate and Otjikoto, and lower royalty costs at Fekola, helped drive lower than expected consolidated cash operating costs and all-in sustaining costs.

At the Fekola Mine, the Company remains focused on efficient operations at both the Fekola and Cardinal open-pits and Fekola underground. In the third quarter of 2026, open pit activities at Fekola transitioned to waste stripping in Phase 8. This large waste mining campaign will continue through the majority of 2027. The issuance of the Menankoto exploitation permit by the State of Mali during the third quarter, which together with the Dandoko exploration permit forms Fekola Regional, unlocks one of the Company's most important near-term growth opportunities. With the Menankoto exploitation permit now received, mining pre-stripping activities commenced in October and ore is expected to be delivered to the Fekola process plant in the first quarter of 2027, upon completion of the toll milling agreement. Fekola Regional is expected to ramp up operations through the end of 2027, and produce in excess of 150,000 ounces of gold per year from 2028 through the mid-2030’s.

At Goose, remediation repairs as a result of the crushing circuit fire have been completed along with Phase 1 of the planned Goose fixed crushing circuit upgrades. Mill throughput is now averaging 3,200 tpd and is expected to remain at those levels until mid-year 2027, at which time the Company expects to complete Phase 2 upgrades in order that the Goose mill operates at an average of 4,000 tonnes per day. B2Gold continues to target gold production of 300,000 ounces of gold per year over the medium-term.

At Masbate, strong gold production results from the first nine months of 2026 are expected to continue through the remainder of the year. As a result, the Company is lowering its 2026 cash operating cost and all-in sustaining cost guidance for Masbate. Ongoing exploration, permitting and mine planning work is underway to evaluate additional opportunities for mine life extensions at current gold prices.

Similarly, at Otjikoto strong gold production results from the first nine months of 2026 are expected to continue throughout the remainder of the year. As a result, the Company is lowering its 2026 all-in sustaining cost guidance for Otjikoto. Work progressed during the quarter at Antelope, four kilometres southwest of Otjikoto, where surface and underground infrastructure is being established to support the development phase of the Antelope deposit.
